exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: The function accepts external input (cookie/query parameter) and uses it directly in a security-sensitive operation (stylesheet selection) without validation against an allowlist of permitted stylesheet titles.

connection.evidence: External input flows from WebUtil.readCookie('stylesheet') or WebUtil.getQueryVar('stylesheet') directly to the sheet parameter, which is used in string comparison with link.title values to enable/disable stylesheets.

diff_causality.evidence: This is an added function that introduces the stylesheet selection capability. Reverting would remove the entire mechanism that allows external input to control stylesheet selection.

security_control.required_control: Input validation against allowlist of permitted stylesheet titles
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-20 requires validation of inputs used in security-sensitive operations. Stylesheet selection affects UI rendering and could enable UI manipulation attacks if arbitrary stylesheets can be activated.
existing_controls_checked: Direct string comparison with link.title values without validation
security_control.deficiency_evidence: The function performs no validation of the sheet parameter against a known allowlist before using it to enable stylesheets. It only checks if the input matches any existing link.title, which may not be restrictive enough.

concrete_impact.evidence: The evidence shows UI manipulation capability but does not demonstrate concrete security impact such as code execution, data access, or data modification. The impact appears limited to visual interface changes.

cwe_assessments.diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the entire stylesheet selection functionality would be removed, eliminating the ability for external input to control which stylesheet is enabled.
